schemas.temporalOwner: namespace Test { entity User; entity Item { owner: User }; action Approve appliesTo { principal: [User], resource: [Item], context: { input: { stock: String } } }; action Sell appliesTo { principal: [User], resource: [Item], context: { input: { stock: String } } }; }

cases.question: A trusted history event whose resource entity lacks the `owner` attribute makes the reference abort the whole authorization while evaluating the policy set against the history event. D3 computes the temporal leaf from the trace and never surfaces a history-event policy error, so D3 authorizes. Must a history-event policy evaluation error abort the current authorization?
